guides.title: Cape Cod Holiday Events 2026: Strolls, Parades, Lights and Markets

facts.q: When is the Falmouth Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: The Falmouth Village Holiday Stroll is Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 4 to 8 PM on Main Street and Queen's Buy Way, with the lighting of the Village Green at 6 PM, according to the Falmouth Chamber of Commerce's tentative 2026 schedule, which it says is subject to change.

facts.q: When is the Falmouth Christmas parade in 2026?
facts.a: Sunday, December 6, 2026, at noon, according to the Falmouth Chamber of Commerce's tentative 2026 schedule. The 63rd annual parade steps off from Dillingham Avenue and Davis Straits and heads along Main Street to the Village Green.

facts.q: When is the Chatham Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Chatham's Christmas by the Sea weekend is Friday through Sunday, December 11–13, 2026, starting with a Friday night Christmas stroll and tree lighting on Main Street, according to the Chatham Chamber of Commerce.

facts.q: When is the Hyannis Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: The organizers' Hyannis Holiday website lists the weekend as Friday and Saturday, December 4–5, 2026, but its event details are still last year's. The Hyannis Main Street Business Improvement District lists Hyannis Holiday on Saturday, December 5, at noon.
sources: Arts Barnstable, Greater Hyannis Civic Association, Hyannis Main Street BID and Love Live Local
Hyannis Main Street Business Improvement District

facts.q: When is the Mashpee Christmas parade in 2026?
facts.a: Saturday, December 12, 2026. Mashpee Commons lists the Mashpee Holiday Stroll followed by the Mashpee Chamber Parade that day from 1 to 7:30 PM at Central Square, 22 Steeple Street.

facts.q: When is the Sandwich Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Sunday, December 13, 2026, from 11 AM to 4 PM. The Sandwich Chamber of Commerce is expanding its annual Village Stroll into a town-wide event this year.

facts.q: When is the Harwich Port Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Friday, December 4, 2026. The Harwich Chamber of Commerce's schedule starts the Harwich Port Stroll at 5:30 PM, the same time as the tree lighting and caroling in Doane Park, and Santa arrives by fire truck at 6:15 PM.

facts.q: When is Holly Folly 2026 in Provincetown?
facts.a: Holly Folly runs all four weekends in December 2026: December 4–6, 11–13, 18–20 and 25–27, according to the Provincetown Business Guild.

facts.q: When is the Pilgrim Monument lighting in 2026?
facts.a: Wednesday, November 25, 2026, Thanksgiving Eve. The Pilgrim Monument and Provincetown Museum's Annual Lighting On The Hill runs from 4 to 5:30 PM, the monument is lit at 5 PM, and the event is free.
Gardens Aglow 2026 at Heritage Museums & Gardens in Sandwich opens November 27 and runs on select nights through December 27, from 4:30 to 8:30 PM with last entry at 8 PM.

facts.q: Is the Polar Express train running on Cape Cod in 2026?
facts.a: Yes. When we checked on November 8, 2026, Cape Cod Central Railroad's Polar Express page said "Tickets for 2026 now available!" The train departs from 70 Main Street in Buzzards Bay, and the ticket page lists an opening-weekend fare valid 11/20–11/22.

guides.title: Whales and Seals on Cape Cod in Winter: Where to Look and How Close You Can Get
keywords: where to see seals on cape cod
best time to see whales off cape cod

facts.q: When is the best time to see right whales on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Right whales typically arrive in Cape Cod Bay in early winter, and many stay through mid-May. April is typically the peak of the season, though in 2025/26 March was the busiest month in Cape Cod Bay.

facts.q: Can you see right whales from shore on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Yes, especially in spring. Right whales often feed very close to shore, offering watchers on the beach unbeatable views, according to the Center for Coastal Studies, and the National Park Service says whales can often be seen from shore at Provincetown's Race Point Beach in spring.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: How close can you get to a right whale?
facts.a: Federal regulations prohibit approaching or remaining within 500 yards (1,500 feet) of a right whale, whether by boat, by aircraft including drones, or on a surfboard, kayak or jet ski, and the Center for Coastal Studies notes the limit applies to paddle-boarders and swimmers too. Massachusetts regulations also bar any vessel in state waters, or registered in Massachusetts, from entering the 500-yard zone around a surfacing right whale. You can still watch from the beach: right whales often feed very close to shore.

facts.q: Where can you see seals on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Monomoy National Wildlife Refuge off Chatham: South Monomoy Island contains the largest gray seal haul-out site on the U.S. Atlantic coast. On the refuge's mainland trails at Morris Island in Chatham, the refuge says you may see "the occasional seal".

facts.q: How far should you stay from seals?
facts.a: NOAA's viewing guideline is at least 150 feet (50 yards), and to limit your viewing to 30 minutes or less. Federal law prohibits harming or harassing them, and feeding them is against the law. Touching or trying to touch a seal violates the Marine Mammal Protection Act.
sources: NOAA Fisheries, Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office

facts.q: Who do I call about a stranded seal or whale on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Call the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) at (508) 743-9548, which covers Cape Cod and southeastern Massachusetts, or NOAA's Northeast Marine Mammal and Sea Turtle Stranding and Entanglement Hotline at (866) 755-6622.

facts.q: What should I do if I find a sea turtle on a Cape Cod beach in winter?
facts.a: Don't put it back in the water, and don't assume it's dead: turtles that look lifeless are often still alive. Mass Audubon asks you to move it above the high tide line without grabbing it by the head or flippers, cover it completely with seaweed (never sand), mark the spot, and call its Wellfleet Bay hotline at 508-349-2615, option 2.
sources: Mass Audubon, Wellfleet Bay Wildlife Sanctuary
